modelEssay.title: The Importance of Motivation and Methods in Learning
modelEssay.content:
Learning is a lifelong journey that requires both motivation and effective methods to be successful. Motivation fuels the desire to learn, while methods provide the roadmap to achieve educational goals.

Firstly, motivation is the driving force behind any educational endeavor. Without it, students may find themselves lacking the necessary enthusiasm to engage with the material, leading to poor performance and even dropping out. For instance, students who are intrinsically motivated to learn a language often excel because they are passionate about the culture and communication it offers. On the other hand, methods are equally crucial as they dictate the efficiency of learning. A student using the Socratic method for critical thinking, for example, may develop a deeper understanding of complex topics compared to rote memorization.

In conclusion, motivation and methods are the twin pillars of effective learning. They complement each other, with motivation providing the will to learn and methods offering the means to do so effectively. Educators and students alike should重视 both aspects to foster a love for learning and achieve academic success.

transcript.text: So, how's our presentation about the restructuring of the company coming along?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 那么，我们关于公司重组的汇报进展如何？

transcript.speaker: F

transcript.text: People are worried about their jobs, too.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 人们也担心他们的工作。

transcript.text: I think we need to stress that while there'll be some job changes, there won't be anyone getting dismissed.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我认为我们需要强调，虽然会有一些工作变动，但不会有人被解雇。

transcript.text: In fact, we're looking to take on more staff.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 事实上，我们计划招聘更多员工。

transcript.text: Agreed.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 同意。

transcript.text: You can hardly blame people for worrying, though.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 然而，你很难责怪人们担心。

transcript.text: We need to make it clear that it's not just change for change's sake.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我们需要明确表示，这不仅仅是为了改变而改变。

transcript.text: In other words, we really must make the case for why we are doing it.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 换句话说，我们必须真正说明我们为什么这样做。

transcript.text: So, what's the outline of the presentation?
transcript.speaker: F

transcript.text: After that, I'll outline the new company structures and who's going where.

transcript.text: Then, I'll hand it over to you to discuss the timeline and summarize, and we'll take questions together at the end.
transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: Anything else?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 还有别的吗？

transcript.text: Oh, yeah.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 哦，对了。

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我们应该让员工知道沟通渠道，你知道，他们可以就这些变革联系谁或向谁提问。

transcript.text: Yes.

transcript.text: And we can collect some frequently asked questions and present some general answers.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我们可以收集一些常见问题并提供一些一般性答案。

transcript.text: Hmm.

transcript.translation: 嗯。

transcript.text: Airline passengers have to deal with a lot these days, getting bumped from flights and losing luggage on top of the general anxiety that nervous passengers always feel.
transcript.translation: 如今，航空公司乘客面临诸多挑战，除了紧张乘客常有的普遍焦虑外，还可能遭遇航班拒载和行李丢失。

transcript.text: At the Cincinnati-Northern Kentucky International Airport, miniature horses deliver a calming force two times a month.
transcript.translation: 在辛辛那提-北肯塔基国际机场，每月两次，迷你马会带来一种安抚力量。

transcript.text: Denver and Ruby are two of the 34 therapy horses brought in from a local farm.
transcript.translation: Denver和Ruby是34匹从当地农场引入的治疗马中的两匹。

transcript.text: They can usually be found in the ticket counter area, interacting with travelers.
transcript.translation: 它们通常可以在售票区找到，与旅客互动。

transcript.text: More than 30 airports across the country now have therapy dogs.
transcript.translation: 全国超过30个机场现在有治疗犬。

transcript.text: San Francisco has a therapy pig.
transcript.translation: 旧金山有一头治疗猪。

transcript.text: San Jose, California, began a dog program after the terrorist attacks of September 11.
transcript.translation: 加利福尼亚州的圣何塞在9月11日恐怖袭击后开始了一个狗项目。

transcript.text: Since its beginning, the program has now grown and has 21 therapy dogs and a therapy cat.
transcript.translation: 自启动以来，该项目现已发展壮大，拥有21只治疗犬和一只治疗猫。

transcript.text: The animals don't get startled.
transcript.translation: 这些动物不会受惊。

transcript.text: They have had hundreds of hours of airport training, so they are used to having luggage and people crowding around them.
transcript.translation: 它们已经接受了数百小时的机场训练，所以习惯了行李和人们在它们周围拥挤。

transcript.text: These professional animals are probably better at finding their way in the airports than the most frequent of travelers.
transcript.translation: 这些专业动物可能在机场里比最频繁的旅客更擅长找路。

transcript.text: The passengers often say that seeing animals makes them feel much better and helps them to calm down before a flight.
transcript.translation: 乘客们常说，看到动物让他们感觉好多了，并帮助他们在飞行前冷静下来。

transcript.text: This little bit of support can sometimes make a big difference.

transcript.text: Some passengers enjoy the animals so much that they call the airport to schedule flights around their visits.
transcript.translation: 一些乘客非常喜欢这些动物，以至于他们打电话给机场，根据动物的访问时间来安排行程。

transcript.text: Visits to nursing homes and schools are also a regular part of the horses' schedule.
transcript.translation: 访问养老院和学校也是这些马匹日程的常规部分。

transcript.text: Their owner is already working on a new idea for a therapy animal, donkeys.
transcript.translation: 它们的主人已经在为一种新的治疗动物——驴——制定新计划。

transcript.text: Hello, viewers!
transcript.translation: 观众朋友们，你们好！

transcript.text: Today, I'm standing at a 2,000-year-old Roman-era site.
transcript.translation: 今天，我站在一个有2000年历史的罗马时代遗址。

transcript.text: Here, the brightly colored scenes that once decorated a mansion are being dug up.
transcript.translation: 在这里，曾经装饰一座豪宅的鲜艳场景正在被发掘。

transcript.text: These scenes are turning up in the southern French city of Arles, surprising the historians who have been working here since 2014.
transcript.translation: 这些场景出现在法国南部城市阿尔勒，令自2014年以来一直在此工作的历史学家们感到惊讶。

transcript.text: Patches of paint still cling to the stone walls of the bedroom and reception hall.
transcript.translation: 卧室和接待厅的石墙上仍然附着着一块块油漆。

transcript.text: Some of these painted walls are preserved in places to a height of one meter.
transcript.translation: 其中一些绘有壁画的墙面在局部保存高达一米。

transcript.text: In addition, thousands of fragments that fell off the walls have been recovered.
transcript.translation: 此外，从墙上掉落的成千上万碎片已被找回。

transcript.text: These pieces have been put back together with great care and display a variety of images.

transcript.text: Some of these images include figures never seen before in France, such as a woman playing a stringed instrument, possibly a character from mythology.

transcript.text: Good afternoon class.
transcript.translation: 下午好，同学们。

transcript.text: Today I want to discuss with you a new approach to empirical research.
transcript.translation: 今天我想和大家讨论一种实证研究的新方法。

transcript.text: In the past, scientists often worked alone.
transcript.translation: 过去，科学家经常独自工作。

transcript.text: They were confined to the university or research center where they worked.
transcript.translation: 他们局限于自己工作的大学或研究中心。

transcript.text: Today, though, we are seeing mergers of some of the greatest scientific minds, regardless of their location.
transcript.translation: 然而今天，我们看到一些最伟大的科学头脑的融合，无论他们身处何地。

transcript.text: There has never been a better time for collaborations with foreign scientists.
transcript.translation: 与外国科学家合作的时机从未如此好过。

transcript.text: In fact, the European Union is taking the lead.
transcript.translation: 事实上，欧盟正在引领潮流。

transcript.text: Spurred on by funding policies, half of European research articles had international co-authors in 2007.
transcript.translation: 在资助政策的推动下，2007年有一半的欧洲研究论文拥有国际合著者。

transcript.text: This is more than twice the level of two decades ago.
transcript.translation: 这是二十年前水平的两倍多。

transcript.text: The European Union's level of international co-authorship is about twice that of the United States, Japan and India.
transcript.translation: 欧盟的国际合作作者水平大约是美国、日本和印度的两倍。

transcript.text: Even so, the levels in these countries are also rising.
transcript.translation: 即便如此，这些国家的水平也在上升。

transcript.text: This is a sign of the continued allure of creating scientific coalitions across borders.
transcript.translation: 这表明跨越国界创建科学联盟的吸引力持续存在。

transcript.text: Andras Schubert, a researcher at the Institute for Science Policy Research, says that the rise in collaboration is partly out of necessity.
transcript.translation: 科学政策研究所的研究员安德拉斯·舒伯特表示，合作的增加部分是由于必要性。

transcript.text: This necessity comes with the rise of big science.
transcript.translation: 这种必要性伴随着大科学的兴起。

transcript.text: Many scientific endeavors have become more complicated.
transcript.translation: 许多科学研究变得更加复杂。

transcript.text: These new complications require the money and labor of many nations.
transcript.translation: 这些新的复杂性需要多国的资金和劳动力。

transcript.text: But, he says, collaborations have also emerged because of increased possibilities.
transcript.translation: 但他说，合作的出现也是由于可能性的增加。

transcript.text: The Internet allows like-minded scientists to find each other.
transcript.translation: 互联网让志同道合的科学家能够找到彼此。

transcript.text: Simultaneously, dramatic drops in communication costs ease long-distance interactions.
transcript.translation: 同时，通信成本的急剧下降使得远距离交流变得容易。

transcript.text: And there's a reward.
transcript.translation: 而且还有回报。

transcript.text: Studies of citation counts show that internationally co-authored papers have better visibility.
transcript.translation: 对引用次数的研究表明，国际合作论文的可见度更高。

transcript.text: Schubert says international collaboration is a way to spread ideas in wider and wider circles.
transcript.translation: 舒伯特说，国际合作是一种将思想传播得越来越广的方式。

transcript.text: Caroline Wagner, a research scientist at George Washington University, notes that international collaborations offer additional flexibility.
transcript.translation: 乔治华盛顿大学的科研人员卡罗琳·瓦格纳指出，国际合作提供了额外的灵活性。

transcript.text: Whereas local collaborations sometimes persist past the point of usefulness because of social or academic obligations, international ones can be cultivated and dropped more freely.
transcript.translation: 而本地合作有时因社会或学术义务而持续超出实用阶段，国际合作则可以更自由地培养和放弃。

transcript.text: The collaborative trend is true across scientific disciplines.
transcript.translation: 合作趋势在所有科学学科中都是真实的。

transcript.text: Some fields, though, have a greater tendency for it.
transcript.translation: 然而，一些领域对此有更大的倾向。

transcript.text: Particle physicists and astronomers collaborate often.
transcript.translation: 粒子物理学家和天文学家经常合作。

transcript.text: This is because they must share expensive facilities.
transcript.translation: 这是因为他们必须共享昂贵的设施。

transcript.text: Mathematicians, by contrast, tend historically towards solitude.
transcript.translation: 相比之下，数学家历史上倾向于独处。

transcript.text: As a consequence, they lag behind other disciplines.
transcript.translation: 因此，他们落后于其他学科。

transcript.text: However, Wagner says, partnerships are rising there, too.
transcript.translation: 然而，瓦格纳说，那里的合作也在增加。

transcript.text: The level of collaboration also varies from country to country.
transcript.translation: 合作水平也因国家而异。

transcript.text: There are historical and political reasons as to why collaborations emerge, says Wagner.
transcript.translation: 瓦格纳说，合作的出现有历史和政治原因。

transcript.text: This rise is also apparently boosted by policies embedded in European framework funding schemes.
transcript.translation: 这种增长显然也受到嵌入欧洲框架资助计划中的政策的推动。

transcript.text: These policies underlie funding requirements that often require teamwork.
transcript.translation: 这些政策构成了资助要求的基础，这些要求通常需要团队合作。

transcript.text: Recording 2.
transcript.translation: 录音二。

transcript.text: Good evening.
transcript.translation: 晚上好。

transcript.text: In 1959, on the day that I was born, a headline in Life magazine proclaimed, Target Venus.
transcript.translation: 1959年，在我出生的那一天，《生活》杂志的一则标题宣称：目标金星。

transcript.text: There may be life there.
transcript.translation: 那里可能有生命。

transcript.text: It told of how scientists rode a balloon to an altitude of 80,000 feet to make telescope observations of Venus' atmosphere and how their discovery of water raised hopes that there could be living things there.
transcript.translation: 它讲述了科学家如何乘坐气球升至80,000英尺的高度，对金星大气层进行望远镜观测，以及他们发现水如何引发了那里可能存在生物的希望。

transcript.text: As a kid, I thrilled to tales of adventure in Isaac Asimov's juvenile science fiction novel Lucky Star and the Oceans of Venus.
transcript.translation: 小时候，我为艾萨克·阿西莫夫的少年科幻小说《幸运星与金星海洋》中的冒险故事而激动。

transcript.text: For many of my peers, though, Venus quickly lost its romance.
transcript.translation: 然而，对许多我的同龄人来说，金星很快失去了它的浪漫色彩。

transcript.text: The very first thing that scientists discovered with a mission to another planet was that Venus was not at all the earthly paradise that fiction had portrayed.
transcript.translation: 科学家通过任务探索其他行星时发现的第一件事是，金星根本不是小说所描绘的人间天堂。

transcript.text: It is nearly identical to our own planet in bulk properties such as mass, density, and size, but its surface has been cooked and dried by an ocean of carbon dioxide.
transcript.translation: 它在质量、密度和大小等整体属性上几乎与我们的地球相同，但其表面被二氧化碳海洋烘烤和干燥。

transcript.text: Trapped in the burning death grip of a runaway greenhouse effect, Venus has long been held up as a cautionary tale for everything that could go wrong on a planet like Earth.
transcript.translation: 被困在失控温室效应的致命炽热掌控中，金星长期以来被视为一个警示故事，提醒在像地球这样的行星上可能发生的一切错误。

transcript.text: As a possible home for alien life, it has been voted the planet least likely to succeed.
transcript.translation: 作为外星生命可能的家园，它被投票为最不可能成功的行星。

transcript.text: But I have refused to give up on Venus, and over the years my stubborn loyalty has been justified.
transcript.translation: 但我拒绝放弃金星，多年来，我固执的忠诚得到了证明。

transcript.text: The rocky views glimpsed by Venera 9 and other Russian landers suggested a tortured volcanic history.
transcript.translation: 金星9号和其他俄罗斯着陆器瞥见的岩石景象暗示了一段坎坷的火山历史。

transcript.text: That was confirmed in the early 1990s by the American Magellan orbiter, which used radar to peer through the planet's thick clouds and map out a rich, varied, and dynamic surface.
transcript.translation: 这在20世纪90年代初被美国麦哲伦轨道器证实，它使用雷达穿透该行星的浓密云层，绘制出丰富、多样且动态的表面地图。

transcript.text: The surface formed mostly in the last billion years, which makes it fresher and more recently active than any rocky planet other than Earth.
transcript.translation: 表面主要在过去十亿年形成，这使得它比除了地球之外的任何岩石行星都更清新、更近期活跃。

transcript.text: Russian and American spacecraft also found hints that its ancient climate might have been wetter, cooler, and possibly even friendly to life.
transcript.translation: 俄罗斯和美国的航天器也发现迹象表明，其古代气候可能更湿润、更凉爽，甚至可能适合生命。

transcript.text: Measurements of density and composition imply that Venus originally formed out of basically the same stuff as Earth.
transcript.translation: 密度和成分的测量表明，金星最初由与地球基本相同的物质形成。

transcript.text: That presumably included much more water than the tiny trace we find blowing in the thick air today.
transcript.translation: 这推测包括比我们今天在浓密空气中发现的微小痕迹更多的水分。

transcript.text: Thus our picture of Venus at around the time life was getting started on Earth is one of warm oceans, probably rich with organic molecules, splashing around rocky shores and volcanic vents.
transcript.translation: 因此，我们在生命在地球上开始时的金星画面是温暖的海洋，可能富含有机分子，在岩石海岸和火山口周围飞溅。

transcript.text: The sun was considerably less bright back then, so Venus was arguably a cozier habitat for life than Earth.
transcript.translation: 那时的太阳要暗得多，因此可以说金星比地球更适合生命栖息。

transcript.text: Recording 3.
transcript.translation: 录音3。

transcript.text: I'm a psychology professor at the University of British Columbia.
transcript.translation: 我是不列颠哥伦比亚大学的心理学教授。

transcript.text: I specialize in cultural psychology, examining similarities and differences between East Asians and North Americans.
transcript.translation: 我专攻文化心理学，研究东亚人和北美人的相似之处和差异。

transcript.text: Our research team has been looking at cultural differences in self-enhancing motivations, how people have positive feelings towards not only themselves, but things connected to themselves.
transcript.translation: 我们的研究团队一直在研究自我提升动机中的文化差异，即人们不仅对自己，而且对与自身相关的事物产生积极情感的方式。

transcript.text: For example, when you own something, you view it as more valuable than when you don't own it.
transcript.translation: 例如，当你拥有某物时，你会认为它比你未拥有时更有价值。

transcript.text: It's called the endowment effect.
transcript.translation: 这被称为禀赋效应。

transcript.text: The strength of that effect is stronger in Western cultures than in East Asian cultures.
transcript.translation: 这种效应在西方文化中比在东亚文化中更强。

transcript.text: So we've been looking at other ways of seeing whether this motivation to view oneself positively is shaped by cultural experiences.
transcript.translation: 因此，我们一直在寻找其他方式，以观察这种积极看待自己的动机是否受文化经历塑造。

transcript.text: We've also started to look at how culture shapes sleep.
transcript.translation: 我们已经开始研究文化如何塑造睡眠。

transcript.text: We are still in the exploratory stages of this project, although what's noteworthy is that East Asians on average sleep about an hour and a half less each night than North Americans do.
transcript.translation: 我们仍处于这个项目的探索阶段，但值得注意的是，东亚人平均每晚比北美人少睡大约一个半小时。

transcript.text: And it's not a more efficient sleep, not like they're compressing relatively more value out of their hours.
transcript.translation: 而且这不是更高效的睡眠，并不是他们从睡眠时间中压缩出相对更多的价值。

transcript.text: Other studies have found that even infants in East Asia sleep about an hour less than European infants.
transcript.translation: 其他研究发现，即使是东亚的婴儿也比欧洲婴儿少睡大约一小时。

transcript.text: So we're trying to figure out how culture shapes the way you sleep.
transcript.translation: 因此，我们正试图弄清文化如何塑造你的睡眠方式。

transcript.text: Our experiment does not take place in a sleep lab.
transcript.translation: 我们的实验不是在睡眠实验室进行的。

transcript.text: Instead, we lend people motion-detecting watches and they wear them for a week at a time.
transcript.translation: 相反，我们借给人们运动检测手表，他们每次佩戴一周。

transcript.text: Whenever they are not having a shower or swimming, they keep it on.
transcript.translation: 只要他们不在淋浴或游泳，他们就一直戴着它。

transcript.text: These kinds of watches are used in sleep studies as a way of measuring how long people are sleeping, how efficient their sleep is, and whether they are waking up in the night.
transcript.translation: 这类手表在睡眠研究中用于测量人们睡眠时长、睡眠效率以及是否夜间醒来。

transcript.text: Ideally, I'd like to take this into a controlled lab environment.
transcript.translation: 理想情况下，我希望将此纳入受控的实验室环境。

transcript.text: We'll see where the research points us.
transcript.translation: 我们将看研究指向何方。

transcript.text: We usually start off with the more affordable methods.
transcript.translation: 我们通常从更经济实惠的方法开始。

transcript.text: And if everything looks promising, then it'll justify trying to build a sleep lab and study sleep across cultures that way.
transcript.translation: 如果一切看起来有希望，那么它将证明尝试建立睡眠实验室并以这种方式跨文化研究睡眠是合理的。

transcript.text: Why do we study sleep?
transcript.translation: 我们为什么研究睡眠？

transcript.text: Sleep is something that has really been an unexplored topic cross-culturally.
transcript.translation: 睡眠在跨文化研究中确实是一个未被探索的话题。

transcript.text: I'm attracted to it because culture isn't something that only shapes the way our minds operate.
transcript.translation: 我对此感兴趣，因为文化不仅仅是塑造我们思维运作方式的事物。

transcript.text: It shapes the way our bodies operate, too, and sleep is at the intersection of those.
transcript.translation: 它也塑造我们身体的运作方式，而睡眠正位于这两者的交汇处。

paragraphs.text: Steel is valued for its reliability, but not when it gets cold. Most forms of steel __26__ become brittle (脆的) at temperatures below about -25℃ unless they are mixed with other metals. Now, though, a novel type of steel has been developed that resists __27__ at much lower temperatures, while retaining its strength and toughness - without the need for expensive __28__.
paragraphs.translation: 钢因其可靠性而备受重视，但在寒冷条件下却不然。大多数形式的钢在低于约-25℃的温度下会突然变脆，除非与其他金属混合。然而，现在已经开发出一种新型钢，它能在更低的温度下抵抗断裂，同时保持其强度和韧性——无需昂贵的添加剂。

paragraphs.text: Steel's fragility at low temperatures first became a major concern during the Second World War. After German U-boats torpedoed (用鱼雷攻击) numerous British ships, a 2700-strong fleet of cheap-and-cheerful "Liberty ships" was introduced to replace the lost vessels, providing a lifeline for the __29__ British. But the steel shells of hundreds of the ships __30__ in the icy north Atlantic, and 12 broke in half and sank.
paragraphs.translation: 钢在低温下的脆性在第二次世界大战期间首次成为主要关注点。在德国U型潜艇用鱼雷击沉众多英国船只后，一支由2700艘廉价而实用的“自由轮”组成的船队被引入以替代损失的船只，为被围困的英国人提供了一条生命线。但是，数百艘船只的钢壳在冰冷的北大西洋中开裂，其中12艘断裂成两半并沉没。

paragraphs.text: Brittleness remains a problem when building steel structures in cold conditions, such as oil rigs in the Arctic. So scientists have __31__ to find a solution by mixing it with expensive metals such as nickel.
paragraphs.translation: 在寒冷条件下建造钢结构时，脆性仍然是一个问题，例如北极的石油钻井平台。因此，科学家们努力寻找解决方案，通过将其与昂贵的金属如镍混合。

paragraphs.text: Yuuji Kimura and colleagues in Japan tried a more physical __32__. Rather than adding other metals, they developed a complex mechanical process involving repeated heating and very severe mechanical deformation, known as tempforming.
paragraphs.translation: 日本的木村裕二及其同事尝试了一种更物理的方法。他们不是添加其他金属，而是开发了一种复杂的机械过程，涉及反复加热和非常剧烈的机械变形，称为热成形。

paragraphs.text: The resulting steel appears to achieve a combination of strength and toughness that is __33__ to that of modern steels that are very rich in alloy content and, therefore, very expensive.
paragraphs.translation: 由此产生的钢似乎实现了强度和韧性的结合，这与合金含量非常高、因此非常昂贵的现代钢相当。

paragraphs.text: Kimura's team intends to use its tempformed steel to make ultra-high strength parts, such as bolts. They hope to reduce both the number of __34__ needed in a construction job and their weight by replacing solid supports with __35__ tubes, for example. This could reduce the amount of steel needed to make everything from automobiles to buildings and bridges.
paragraphs.translation: 木村团队打算使用其热成形钢制造超高强度部件，如螺栓。他们希望通过用空心管替换实心支撑等方式，减少建筑作业中所需的部件数量及其重量。这可以减少制造从汽车到建筑和桥梁所需的一切的钢材用量。

questionGroups.title: The future of personal satellite technology is here—are we ready for it?

material.title: The future of personal satellite technology is here—are we ready for it?

paragraphs.text: Satellites used to be the exclusive playthings of rich governments and wealthy corporations. But increasingly, as space becomes more democratized, they are coming within reach of ordinary people. Just like drones (无人机) before them, miniature satellites are beginning to fundamentally transform our conceptions of who gets to do what up above our heads.
paragraphs.translation: 卫星曾经是富裕政府和富有公司的专属玩物。但随着太空日益民主化，它们正逐渐进入普通人的视野。就像之前的无人机一样，微型卫星正开始从根本上改变我们对于谁能在头顶上做什么的观念。

paragraphs.text: As a recent report from the National Academy of Sciences highlights, these satellites hold tremendous potential for making satellite-based science more accessible than ever before. However, as the cost of getting your own satellite in orbit drops sharply, the risks of irresponsible use grow. The question here is no longer "Can we?" but "Should we?" What are the potential downsides of having a slice of space densely populated by equipment built by people not traditionally labeled as "professionals"? And what would the responsible and beneficial development and use of this technology actually look like? Some of the answers may come from a nonprofit organization that has been building and launching amateur satellites for nearly 50 years.
paragraphs.translation: 正如国家科学院最近的一份报告所强调的，这些卫星在使卫星科学比以往任何时候都更易获取方面具有巨大潜力。然而，随着将个人卫星送入轨道的成本急剧下降，不负责任使用所带来的风险也在增加。这里的问题不再是“我们能吗？”而是“我们应该吗？”如果一小块太空被非传统“专业人士”建造的设备密集占据，潜在的弊端是什么？负责任且有益的技术开发和使用究竟是什么样子？一些答案可能来自一个近50年来一直建造和发射业余卫星的非营利组织。

paragraphs.text: Having your personal satellite launched into orbit might sound like an idea straight out of science fiction. But over the past few decades a unique class of satellites has been created that fits the bill: CubeSats. The "Cube" here simply refers to the satellite's shape. The most common CubeSat is a 10cm cube, so small that a single CubeSat could easily be mistaken for a paperweight on your desk. These mini-satellites can fit in a launch vehicle's formerly "wasted space." Multiples can be deployed in combination for more complex missions than could be achieved by one CubeSat alone.
paragraphs.translation: 将个人卫星发射到轨道听起来像是科幻小说中的想法。但在过去几十年里，一种独特的卫星类别被创造出来，符合这一要求：立方体卫星（CubeSats）。这里的“立方体”仅指卫星的形状。最常见的立方体卫星是一个10厘米的立方体，小到单个立方体卫星很容易被误认为是桌上的镇纸。这些微型卫星可以装入运载火箭中原本“浪费的空间”。多个卫星可以组合部署，执行比单个立方体卫星更复杂的任务。

paragraphs.text: Within their compact bodies these minute satellites are able to house sensors and communications receivers/transmitters that enable operators to study Earth from space, as well as space around Earth. They're primarily designed for Low Earth Orbit (LEO) - an easily accessible region of space from around 200 to 800 miles above Earth, where human-tended missions like the Hubble Space Telescope and the International Space Station (ISS) hang out. But they can attain more distant orbits; NASA plans for most of its future Earth-escaping payloads (to the moon and Mars especially) to carry CubeSats.
paragraphs.translation: 在这些紧凑的内部，这些微小的卫星能够容纳传感器和通信接收器/发射器，使操作员能够从太空研究地球以及地球周围的太空。它们主要设计用于近地轨道（LEO）——一个距离地球约200至800英里的易达太空区域，哈勃太空望远镜和国际空间站（ISS）等载人任务都在此进行。但它们也能到达更远的轨道；NASA计划其未来大多数脱离地球的有效载荷（特别是前往月球和火星的）携带立方体卫星。

paragraphs.text: Because they're so small and light, it costs much less to get a CubeSat into Earth's orbit than a traditional communications or GPS satellite. For instance, a research group here at Arizona State University recently claimed their developmental small CubeSats could cost as little as $3,000 to put in orbit. This decrease in cost allows researchers, hobbyists and even elementary school groups to put simple instruments into LEO or even having them deployed from the ISS.
paragraphs.translation: 由于它们非常小和轻，将立方体卫星送入地球轨道的成本远低于传统通信或GPS卫星。例如，亚利桑那州立大学的一个研究小组最近声称，他们开发的小型立方体卫星进入轨道的成本可能低至3000美元。成本的降低使得研究人员、爱好者甚至小学生团体能够将简单仪器送入近地轨道，甚至从国际空间站部署它们。

paragraphs.text: The first CubeSat was created in the early 2000s, as a way of enabling Stanford graduate students to design, build, test and operate a spacecraft with similar capabilities to the USSR's Sputnik (前苏联的人造卫星). Since then, NASA, the National Reconnaissance Office and even Boeing have all launched and operated CubeSats. There are more than 130 currently in operation. The NASA Educational Launch of Nano Satellite program, which offers free launches for educational groups and science missions, is now open to U.S. nonprofit corporations as well. Clearly, satellites are not just for rocket scientists anymore.
paragraphs.translation: 第一个立方体卫星创建于21世纪初，目的是让斯坦福大学的研究生能够设计、建造、测试和操作一个具有类似前苏联人造卫星（Sputnik）能力的航天器。自那时起，NASA、国家侦察局甚至波音都发射和操作了立方体卫星。目前有超过130个在运行。NASA的纳米卫星教育发射计划，为教育团体和科学任务提供免费发射，现在也对美国非营利公司开放。显然，卫星不再仅仅是火箭科学家的专利。

paragraphs.text: The National Academy of Sciences report emphasizes CubeSats' importance in scientific discovery and the training of future space scientists and engineers. Yet it also acknowledges that widespread deployment of LEO CubeSats isn't risk-free. The greatest concern the authors raise is space debris - pieces of "junk" that orbit the earth, with the potential to cause serious damage if they collide with operational units, including the ISS.
paragraphs.translation: 国家科学院的报告强调了立方体卫星在科学发现和培养未来太空科学家与工程师方面的重要性。然而，它也承认近地轨道立方体卫星的广泛部署并非没有风险。作者提出的最大担忧是太空碎片——环绕地球运行的“垃圾”碎片，如果与操作中的设备（包括国际空间站）相撞，可能造成严重损害。

paragraphs.text: Currently, there aren't many CubeSats and they're tracked closely. Yet as LEO opens up to more amateur satellites, they may pose an increasing threat. As the report authors point out, even near-misses might lead to the "creation of a burdensome regulatory framework and affect the future disposition of science CubeSats."
paragraphs.translation: 目前，立方体卫星数量不多，并且受到密切跟踪。然而，随着近地轨道向更多业余卫星开放，它们可能构成日益增长的威胁。正如报告作者所指出的，即使近乎失手的事件也可能导致“创建繁琐的监管框架，并影响未来科学立方体卫星的部署。”

paragraphs.text: CubeSat researchers suggest that now's the time to ponder unexpected and unintended possible consequences of more people than ever having access to their own small slice of space. In an era when you can simply buy a CubeSat kit off the shelf, how can we trust the satellites over our heads were developed with good intentions by people who knew what they were doing? Some "expert amateurs" in the satellite game could provide some inspiration for how to proceed responsibly.
paragraphs.translation: 立方体卫星研究人员建议，现在是思考比以往更多人能访问自己的一小块太空所带来的意外和无意后果的时候了。在一个你可以直接购买立方体卫星套件的时代，我们如何信任头顶上的卫星是由懂行的人怀着善意开发的？卫星领域的一些“专家爱好者”可以为如何负责任地前进提供一些灵感。

paragraphs.text: In 1969, the Radio Amateur Satellite Corporation (AMSAT) was created in order to foster ham radio enthusiasts' (业余无线电爱好者) participation in space research and communication. It continued the efforts, begun in 1961, by Project OSCAR- a U.S.-based group that built and launched the very first nongovernmental satellite just four years after Sputnik. As an organization of volunteers, AMSAT was putting "amateur" satellites in orbit decades before the current CubeSat craze. And over time, its members have learned a thing or two about responsibility. Here, open source development has been a central principle. Within the organization, AMSAT has a philosophy of open sourcing everything, making technical data on all aspects of their satellites fully available to everyone in the organization, and when possible, the public. According to a member of the team responsible for FOX 1-A, AMSAT's first CubeSat, this means that there's no way to sneak something like explosives or an energy emitter into an amateur satellite when everyone has access to the designs and implementation.
paragraphs.translation: 1969年，业余无线电卫星公司（AMSAT）成立，以促进业余无线电爱好者参与太空研究和通信。它延续了1961年由OSCAR项目开始的努力——一个美国团体在人造卫星发射仅四年后就建造并发射了第一颗非政府卫星。作为一个志愿者组织，AMSAT在当前立方体卫星热潮的数十年前就已经将“业余”卫星送入轨道。随着时间的推移，其成员学到了一些关于责任的知识。在这里，开源开发一直是一个核心原则。在组织内部，AMSAT有一种开源一切的哲学，使卫星各方面的技术数据对组织内的每个人公开，并在可能的情况下向公众公开。根据负责FOX 1-A（AMSAT的第一个立方体卫星）的团队成员表示，这意味着当每个人都能访问设计和实施时，无法偷偷将爆炸物或能量发射器之类的设备放入业余卫星。

paragraphs.text: However, they're more cautious about sharing information with nonmembers, as the organization guards against others developing the ability to hijack and take control of their satellites. This form of "self-governance" is possible within long-standing amateur organizations that, over time, are able to build a sense of responsibility to community members, as well as society in general. But what happens when new players emerge, who don't have deep roots within the existing culture?
paragraphs.translation: 然而，他们对与非成员共享信息更为谨慎，因为该组织防范他人开发劫持和控制其卫星的能力。这种“自治”形式在长期存在的业余组织中是可能的，这些组织随着时间的推移，能够培养对社区成员以及整个社会的责任感。但当新玩家出现，而他们没有在现有文化中深深扎根时，会发生什么？

paragraphs.text: Hobbyists and students are gaining access to technologies without being part of a long-standing amateur establishment. They're still constrained by funders, launch providers and a series of regulations - all of which rein in what CubeSat developers can and cannot do. But there's a danger they're ill-equipped to think through potential unintended consequences. What these unintended consequences might be is admittedly far from clear. Yet we know innovators can be remarkably creative with taking technologies in unexpected directions. Think of something as seemingly benign as the cellphone - we have microfinance and text-based social networking at one end of the spectrum, and improvised (临时制作的) explosive devices at the other.
paragraphs.translation: 爱好者和学生正在获取技术，而无需成为长期业余组织的一部分。他们仍然受到资助者、发射提供商和一系列法规的限制——所有这些都约束了立方体卫星开发者的能做和不能做。但存在一种危险，即他们缺乏能力去思考潜在的无意后果。诚然，这些无意后果可能是什么远未明确。然而，我们知道创新者能够非常创造性地将技术引向意想不到的方向。想想像手机这样看似无害的东西——光谱的一端是微金融和基于文本的社交网络，另一端是临时制作的爆炸装置。

paragraphs.text: This is where a culture of social responsibility around CubeSats becomes important - not simply to ensure that physical risks are minimized, but to engage with a much larger community in anticipating and managing less obvious consequences of the technology. This is not an easy task. Yet the evidence from AMSAT and other areas of technology development suggests that responsible amateur communities can and do emerge around novel technologies. The challenge here, of course, is ensuring that what an amateur community considers to be responsible, actually is. Here's where there needs to be a much wider public conversation that extends beyond government agencies and scientific communities to include students, hobbyists, and anyone who may potentially stand to be affected by the use of CubeSat technology.
paragraphs.translation: 这就是围绕立方体卫星的社会责任文化变得重要的地方——不仅仅是为了确保物理风险最小化，还要与更广泛的社区合作，预见和管理技术的不太明显的后果。这不是一项容易的任务。然而，来自AMSAT和技术发展其他领域的证据表明，围绕新技术，负责任的业余社区能够且确实会出现。这里的挑战当然是确保业余社区认为负责任的东西，实际上确实如此。这里需要一场更广泛的公众对话，超越政府机构和科学界，包括学生、爱好者以及任何可能受立方体卫星技术使用影响的人。

questionGroups.title: Passage One

paragraphs.text: When I re-entered the full-time workforce a few years ago after a decade of solitary self-employment, there was one thing I was looking forward to the most: the opportunity to have work friends once again. It wasn't until I entered the corporate world that I realized, for me at least, being friends with colleagues didn't emerge as a priority at all. This is surprising when you consider the prevailing emphasis by scholars and trainers and managers on the importance of cultivating close interpersonal relationships at work. So much research has explored the way in which collegial (同事的) ties can help overcome a range of workplace issues affecting productivity and the quality of work output such as team-based conflict, jealousy, undermining, anger, and more.
paragraphs.translation: 几年前，当我重新进入全职工作领域，结束了十年的个人创业后，我最期待的一件事就是再次拥有工作伙伴。直到我进入企业界才意识到，至少对我来说，与同事成为朋友根本不是优先考虑的事情。当你想到学者、培训师和经理们普遍强调在工作中培养密切人际关系的重要性时，这令人惊讶。许多研究探讨了同事关系如何帮助克服一系列影响生产力和工作产出质量的工作场所问题，如团队冲突、嫉妒、暗中破坏、愤怒等。

paragraphs.text: Perhaps my expectations of lunches, water-cooler gossip and caring, deep-and-meaningful conversations were a legacy of the last time I was in that kind of office environment. Whereas now, as I near the end of my fourth decade, I realize work can be fully functional and entirely fulfilling without needing to be best mates with the people sitting next to you.
paragraphs.translation: 也许我对午餐、茶水间闲聊以及关怀、深入而有意义对话的期望，是我上次在那种办公室环境中的遗留产物。而现在，当我接近四十岁末尾时，我意识到工作可以完全高效且令人满足，而不需要与坐在旁边的人成为好朋友。

paragraphs.text: In an academic analysis just published in the profoundly-respected Journal of Management, researchers have looked at the concept of "indifferent relationships". It's a simple term that encapsulates (概括) the fact that relationships at work can reasonably be non-intimate, inconsequential, unimportant and even, dare I say it, disposable or substitutable.
paragraphs.translation: 在最近发表在备受尊敬的《管理学杂志》上的一项学术分析中，研究人员研究了“冷漠关系”的概念。这是一个简单的术语，概括了工作中关系可以合理地是非亲密的、无关紧要的、不重要的，甚至，我敢说，一次性的或可替代的事实。

paragraphs.text: Indifferent relationships are neither positive nor negative. The limited research conducted thus far indicates they're especially dominant among those who value independence over cooperation, and harmony over confrontation. Indifference is also the preferred option among those who are socially lazy. Maintaining relationships over the long term takes effort. For some of us, too much effort.
paragraphs.translation: 冷漠关系既不是积极的，也不是消极的。迄今为止进行的有限研究表明，它们在重视独立而非合作、重视和谐而非对抗的人群中尤为突出。冷漠也是那些社交懒惰者的首选选择。长期维持关系需要努力。对我们有些人来说，努力太多了。

paragraphs.text: As noted above, indifferent relationships may not always be the most helpful approach in resolving some of the issues that pop up at work. But there are nonetheless several empirically proven benefits. One of those is efficiency. Less time chatting and socializing means more time working and churning (产出).
paragraphs.translation: 如上所述，冷漠关系可能并不总是在解决工作中突然出现的一些问题时最有帮助的方法。但尽管如此，有几个经验证明的好处。其中之一是效率。更少的聊天和社交时间意味着更多的工作和产出时间。

paragraphs.text: The other is self-esteem. As human beings, we're primed to compare ourselves to each other in what is an anxiety-inducing phenomenon. Apparently, we look down on acquaintances more so than friends. Since the former is most common among those inclined towards indifferent relationships, their predominance can bolster individuals' sense of self-worth.
paragraphs.translation: 另一个是自尊。作为人类，我们倾向于相互比较，这是一种引发焦虑的现象。显然，我们比朋友更看不起熟人。由于前者在那些倾向于冷漠关系的人中最常见，他们的主导地位可以增强个人的自我价值感。

paragraphs.text: Ego aside, a third advantage is that the emotional neutrality of indifferent relationships has been found to enhance critical evaluation, to strengthen one's focus on task resolution, and to gain greater access to valuable information. None of that might be as fun as after-work socializing but, hey, I'll take it anyway.
paragraphs.translation: 自尊心暂且不论，第三个优势是冷漠关系的情感中立性被发现可以增强批判性评估，加强对任务解决的专注，并获得更多有价值信息。这些可能都不如下班后社交有趣，但嘿，我还是会接受它。

questionGroups.title: Passage Two

paragraphs.text: In a few decades, artificial intelligence (AI) will surpass many of the abilities that we believe make us special. This is a grand challenge for our age and it may require an "irrational" response.
paragraphs.translation: 在几十年内，人工智能（AI）将超越许多我们认为使我们独特的方面。这是我们这个时代的一个重大挑战，可能需要一种“非理性”的回应。

paragraphs.text: One of the most significant pieces of news from the US in early 2017 was the efforts of Google to make autonomous driving a reality. According to a report, Google's self-driving cars clocked 1,023,330 km, and required human intervention 124 times. That is one intervention about every 8,047 km of autonomous driving. But even more impressive is the progress in just a single year: human interventions fell from 0.8 times per thousand miles to 0.2, a 400% improvement. With such progress, Google's cars will easily surpass my own driving ability later this year.
paragraphs.translation: 2017年初美国最重要的新闻之一是谷歌为使自动驾驶成为现实所作的努力。据报道，谷歌的自动驾驶汽车行驶了1,023,330公里，需要人工干预124次。这大约是每8,047公里自动驾驶就有一次干预。但更令人印象深刻的是仅仅一年内的进步：人工干预从每千英里0.8次降至0.2次，提升了400%。凭借这样的进步，谷歌的汽车将在今年晚些时候轻松超越我自己的驾驶能力。

paragraphs.text: Driving once seemed to be a very human skill. But we said that about chess, too. Then a computer beat the human world champion, repeatedly. The board game Go (围棋) took over from chess as a new test for human thinking in 2016, when a computer beat one of the world's leading professional Go players. With computers conquering what used to be deeply human tasks, what will it mean in the future to be human? I worry about my six-year-old son. What will his place be in a world where machines beat us in one area after another? He'll never calculate faster, never drive better, or even fly more safely. Actually, it all comes down to a fairly simple question: What's so special about us? It can't be skills like arithmetic, which machines already excel in. So far, machines have a pretty hard time emulating creativity, arbitrary enough not to be predicted by a computer, and yet more than simple randomness.
paragraphs.translation: 驾驶曾经似乎是一项非常人性化的技能。但我们对国际象棋也曾这样说。然后计算机多次击败人类世界冠军。在2016年，围棋取代国际象棋成为对人类思维的新测试，当时计算机击败了世界顶尖的专业围棋选手之一。随着计算机征服了曾经深具人性化的任务，未来做人意味着什么？我担心我六岁的儿子。在一个机器在一个又一个领域击败我们的世界里，他的位置在哪里？他永远不会计算得更快，永远不会驾驶得更好，甚至永远不会飞得更安全。实际上，这一切归结为一个相当简单的问题：我们有什么特别之处？不可能是算术这类技能，机器已经擅长这些。到目前为止，机器在模拟创造力方面相当困难，创造力足够任意，无法被计算机预测，但又不仅仅是简单的随机性。

paragraphs.text: Perhaps, if we continue to improve information-processing machines, we'll soon have helpful rational assistants. So we must aim to complement the rationality of the machine, rather than to compete with it. If I'm right, we should foster a creative spirit because a dose of illogical creativity will complement the rationality of the machine. Unfortunately, however, our education system has not caught up to the approaching reality. Indeed, our schools and universities are structured to mould pupils to be mostly obedient servants of rationality, and to develop outdated skills in interacting with outdated machines. We need to help our children learn how to best work with smart computers to improve human decision-making. But most of all we need to keep the long-term perspective in mind: that even if computers will outsmart us, we can still be the most creative. Because if we aren't, we won't be providing much value in future ecosystems, and that may put in question the foundation for our existence.
paragraphs.translation: 也许，如果我们继续改进信息处理机器，我们很快就会拥有有用的理性助手。因此，我们的目标应该是补充机器的理性，而不是与之竞争。如果我是对的，我们应该培养创造精神，因为一剂非理性的创造力将补充机器的理性。然而，不幸的是，我们的教育体系还没有跟上即将到来的现实。确实，我们的学校和大学被构造成培养学生成为理性顺从的仆人，并培养与过时机器互动的过时技能。我们需要帮助我们的孩子学习如何最好地与智能计算机合作，以改善人类的决策。但最重要的是，我们需要保持长远的视角：即使计算机将超越我们，我们仍然可以是最具创造力的。因为如果我们不是，我们在未来的生态系统中将不会提供太多价值，这可能会质疑我们存在的基础。

wrongOptions.A: 虽然文章提到谷歌的实验无人驾驶汽车需要很少的人工干预，但A选项没有涵盖文章强调的进步速度，所以A选项错误。
wrongOptions.B: 文章中并没有提到谷歌的汽车在仅仅一年内就超过了作者的驾驶能力，所以B选项错误。
wrongOptions.D: 文章没有提到谷歌成为自动驾驶领域的世界领导者，所以D选项错误。

questions.questionText: What do we learn from the passage about creativity?

options.label: A
options.text: It is rational.

options.label: B
options.text: It is predictable.

options.label: C
options.text: It is human specific.

options.label: D
options.text: It is yet to be emulated by AI.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章中提到'So far, machines have a pretty hard time emulating creativity, arbitrary enough not to be predicted by a computer, and yet more than simple randomness.'这句话说明创造力是人工智能尚未模仿的人类特质，因此D选项是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: 文章中提到创造力不是理性的，所以A选项错误。
wrongOptions.B: 文章中提到创造力是不可预测的，所以B选项错误。
wrongOptions.C: 文章没有提到创造力是人类特有的，所以C选项错误。

questions.questionText: What should schools help children do in the era of AI?

options.label: A
options.text: Cultivate original thinking.

options.label: B
options.text: Learn to work independently.

options.label: C
options.text: Compete with smart machines.

options.label: D
options.text: Understand howAI works.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章中提到'So we must aim to complement the rationality of the machine, rather than to compete with it. If I'm right, we should foster a creative spirit because a dose of illogical creativity will complement the rationality of the machine.'这句话强调了在人工智能时代，学校应该帮助孩子们培养原创思维，因此A选项是正确答案。

wrongOptions.B: 文章没有提到学校应该帮助孩子们学会独立工作，所以B选项错误。
wrongOptions.C: 文章中提到我们应该补充机器的理性，而不是与之竞争，所以C选项错误。
wrongOptions.D: 虽然理解AI的工作原理很重要，但文章强调的是培养创造性思维，所以D选项错误。

questions.questionText: How can we humans justify our future existence?

options.label: A
options.text: By constantly outsmarting computers.

options.label: B
options.text: By adopting a long-term perspective.

options.label: C
options.text: By rationally compromising with AI.

options.label: D
options.text: By providing value with our creativity.

questions.analysis: 这是一道推理判断题。文章最后一段提到'Because if we aren't, we won't be providing much value in future ecosystems, and that may put in question the foundation for our existence.'这句话暗示了如果我们不能通过创造力提供价值，我们的存在基础可能会受到质疑，因此D选项是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: 文章没有提到人类需要不断地比计算机更聪明，所以A选项错误。
wrongOptions.B: 虽然文章提到了长期视角，但B选项没有涵盖文章的核心观点，所以B选项错误。
wrongOptions.C: 文章中提到我们应该补充机器的理性，而不是与之妥协，所以C选项错误。

questionGroups.sourceText: 汉语现在是世界上用作本族语人数最多的语言。汉语与西方语言的一个重要区别在于它是以方块字(character)而不是以字母构成的。目前仍在使用的书写系统中，汉语是最古老的。在中国，来自不同地区的人可能听不懂对方的方言，但由于汉字有统一的书写形式，他们交流起来几乎没有任何困难。汉语历史上对团结中华民族发挥了重要作用。今天，随着中国经济的快速增长和全球影响力的增强，越来越多其他国家的人也开始学习汉语。

answer.modelTranslation: Mandarin is now the language with the largest number of native speakers in the world. An important distinction between Mandarin and Western languages is that it is composed of characters rather than alphabets. Among the writing systems still in use today, Mandarin is the oldest. In China, people from different regions may not understand each other's dialects, but due to the standardized form of Chinese characters, they can communicate with almost no difficulty. Historically, Mandarin has played a significant role in uniting the Chinese nation. Today, with the rapid growth of China's economy and the enhancement of its global influence, more and more people from other countries are also beginning to learn Mandarin.
translationNotes: 注意'本族语'的翻译，可译为native speakers
'方块字'译为'characters'，注意英文中对汉字的称呼

注意时态的选择，此处用现在时表示客观事实

正确表达'以方块字构成'
